newsitem.title: TURKEY: TURK SHARES DROP 1.52 PCT IN PROFIT-TAKING.
newsitem.headline: TURK SHARES DROP 1.52 PCT IN PROFIT-TAKING.

text.p: Istanbul shares fell in expected profit-taking on Friday morning after Thursday's 5.43 percent jump and amid rising doubts ahead of a censure motion expected to be debated in parliament next week against the Islamist-led coalition, brokers said.

The IMKB National-100 ended 23 points, or 1.52 percent lower at 1,492 after diving to 1,481 from a high of 1,531. Morning volume was little changed at 10.29 trillion lira after Thursday's 10.28 trillion.

"Sales were expected today after the three-day rises. Disciplinary action against dissident MP Yalim Erez by his party and the censure motion irritated the market," said Fuat Akman from Sahin securities.
Four ratified opposition parties submitted a censure motion to topple Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's coalition government.
The index had soared 8.6 percent in the past three days on the rising prospect of a new secularist alliance to replace the ruling Islamist-conservative coalition.

Erez, a former minister of the conservative True Path Party (DYP) has been the chief coordinator of the move to unseat the government. But a disciplionary move was started against Erez on Thursday which could result in his sacking from the party.
It is not clear how many DYP deputies will support the censure motion which needs an absolute majority of 276 votes.

Of the 245 shares traded, falls outdid rises sharply by 158 to 35 and 52 were stable. The IMKB Industrial dropped 1.5 percent to 1,440, the IMKB Services lost 1.65 percent to 1,371 and the IMKB Financial eased 1.26 percent to 1,650.
